summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, alcoholic cirrhosis, Crohn’s disease, and prior spinal surgery was admitted for worsening left leg pain and found to have acute kidney injury and encephalopathy. Initial evaluation revealed hyponatremia, metabolic acidosis, and a urine infection with ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli, treated with IV ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral Macrobid. Her mental status improved with reduction of narcotic and gabapentin dosing. MRI of the spine showed stable post-surgical changes with persistent neuroforaminal narrowing, and lower extremity ultrasound ruled out DVT. She experienced an episode of atypical chest pain, determined to be musculoskeletal, and was started on Imdur for blood pressure and cardiac management. Kidney function returned to baseline with IV fluids and temporary discontinuation of torsemide, which was restarted at a lower dose. She was discharged home with optimized pain control, including reduced OxyContin and continuation of lidocaine patches, and instructions to complete her antibiotic course.
